The '''1935–36 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Madrid Football Club]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|34th season]] in existence, and their [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|8th consecutive season]] in the [[La Liga|Primera División]]. The club also played in the [[Campeonato Regional Centro|Campeonato Regional Mancomunado]] (Joint Regional Championship) and the [[Copa del Rey|Copa del Presidente de la República]] (President of the Republic's Cup).

==Summary==
During the summer, the Spanish Football Federation authorized teams to line-up two foreign players in La Liga matches. The club proceeded to finish second behind champions Athletic Bilbao, despite an excellent offensive performance led by forward [[Fernando Sañudo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/ni-mas-ni-menos/2015/03/01/fernando-sanudo-el-nino-de-los-pies-de.html|title=Fernando Sañudo, Golden Feet Boy|publisher=marca.com|date=1 March 2015|accessdate=24 December 2020|language=es}}</ref>

Meanwhile, in the [[1936 Copa del Presidente de la República|Spanish Cup]] Real Madrid defeated Barcelona in the final on 21 June 1936 to win its seventh title,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/tirandoadar/2011/04/20/el-madrid-barca-de-1936.html|title=The Madrid-Barca of 1936|publisher=marca.com|date=20 April 2011|accessdate=20 December 2020|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://copadelrey.rfef.es/historia-del-campeonato-de-espana/1936-la-ultima-final-antes-de-la-guerra-civil/|title=The Last Final before the Civil War|publisher=rfef.es|date=20 April 2011|accessdate=20 December 2020|language=es}}</ref> with captain Ricardo Zamora producing a superb performance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/fotos/final-del-campeonato-de-espana-de-1936-entre-el-real-madrid-y-el-17354083.html|title=1936: The Last Save by Zamora|publisher=abc.es|date=20 April 2014|accessdate=20 December 2020|language=es}}</ref>

During the autumn of 1936, the [[Siege of Madrid]] started a three-year chapter of the [[Spanish Civil War]] with attacks between the [[Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)|Republican forces]] and [[Nationalist faction (Spanish Civil War)|Nationalist forces]]. The Chamartín Stadium was occupied by the Republicans, and the club suspended activities, which would be resumed in 1939 after the Nationalist victory in the war.
